Commentary.Commentary: England now will look to bat long, their first aim will be to not lose wickets in this final session. Ireland on the other hand, will need a few before Stumps. Can they fight back or will England continue to dominate? We will find out.

For England, thir bowlers were on point. The decision to bowl first has been justified. Stuart Broad was the pick with a five-fer but all their bowlers bowled really well. Josh Tongue did not pick a wicket but was quite sharp and did cause some troubles. Stokes though will be very pleased with where his team stands.

England did not take long to take the remaining wickets after the break! It was Stuart Broad who got the better of Adair and once that stand between Mark and Curtis Campher was broken, wickets fell quickly. Campher followed and then the lower order did not contribute a lot. Overall it was a poor batting display by the Irish. A few of them got off to starts but none went onto make it into a big one. They needed someone to go big but that was missing and they have been bundled out for a poor first innings total.

OUT! TAKEN! Matthew Potts has the last wicket! Length and on off, this one lands and comes back in. Fionn Hand looks to put bat on ball but it takes the inside edge and goes to the left of the keeper who dives and takes it. IRELAND HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 172!

... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Another really good session for England and they are well on top in this game! First, they got rid of the well-set James McCollum and then the big wicket of Tector. Andy McBrine showed some resilliance but he then fell too. However, Curtis Campher is doing well but he will need someone to hang in there with him. Mark Adair has done a decent job so far but can he continue the good work? England on the other hand, will want to continue the same. They will be eager to get the remaining wickets quickly. Can they keep Ireland under 200 or will the Irish cross that mark? Join us in a bit after the break.
On the stumps, kept out. THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: Back for the second session. Ben Stokes leads his team out in the middle. Lorcan Tucker and James McCollum to resume their batting. Stuart Broad to bowl.
...Day 1, Session 2...

The home team bossed the first session. Four wickets in the session and England will happily take it. There was not much swing but some smart cricket from Stuart Broad rewarded him with 3 wickets in no time. He almost had Paul Stirling as well but the review saved him. For Ireland, once they weathered the early storm, McCollum and Paul Stirling played sensibly to build a stand. It was cut short though as Jack Leach struck later on. James McCollum is batting really well as he still waits for a partner to build a big stand. Ireland will hope Lorcan Tucker comes to the rescue as the visitors will look for a much better second session while England will hope to keep bowling in the right areas and clinch more wickets. Stay tuned.
Fuller and outside off. Lorcan Tucker lets it go. That will be LUNCH.

Hello and welcome to the only Test between England and Ireland. After a break off, we are back with the longest format of the game and what better than to kick off at the Home of Cricket, Lord’s! England are clearly the favourites to win against the minnows Ireland who are still new to this format. They though have shown promising signs in their last series against the Lankans and will be truly up for this massive challenge. England have already released their playing side. Josh Tongue is all set to make his debut while Jonny Bairstow will be back on the ground after being sidelined due to injury. Let's hope for an exciting match. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.
